statusText: Tail risk low at 12%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Stress rises to 49% as Asian cash weakens, crude firms again and the long end holds near multi-decade highs.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with Tail well below the block threshold. The narrow danger window spans the 13:30Z US cash open through 15:00Z, where an opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the first meaningful Tail evidence. The 17:00Z 30-Year Bond Auction is the clearest delayed-second-leg mechanism later in the window. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a narrow two-way overnight band while Asian cash weakens and crude firms
body: Oct 7 US cash closed at 31,160.08, -0.21%, after a dip to 30,904.46 was fully retraced into a close only 10 points under the 31,170.12 session high. That completed retracement remains the central Tail-negative observation. Two Globex hours are now observed: NQ Dec26 trades near 31,392.50, -0.03% against a 31,402.25 prior close, inside an 87-point 31,372.25-31,459.00 band. The band low has extended about 27 points versus the prior hour, but price sits mid-range with no directional efficiency, no repeated extension and no failed retracement. VIX settled at 15.08 after a 16.01 intraday print. The new development this hour is Asian cash weakness: the Nikkei 225 trades at 69,259.84, -1.11%, close to its 69,195.47 session low, a second consecutive decline after Oct 7 closed down 0.92% on rising JGB yields and AI/chip profit-taking. That weakness has not transmitted to NQ, which is the material point. The macro backdrop stays more stressed than the price path. FOMC minutes released Oct 7 showed most participants judging that another increase in the federal funds target range would likely be appropriate by year end, after the September 15-16 hike to 3.75-4.00%. The 10Y closed at 5.28% having reached 5.36% intraday, its highest since April 2002, and the 30Y closed at 5.66% after 5.73%, its highest since May 2002; H.15 carries the 2Y at 4.79% for Oct 6. Crude firmed further into this hour, with Brent at 101.77, +1.56%, and WTI at 89.36, +1.22%, against reported Strait of Hormuz attacks and Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure. Under the repository contract this combination of hawkish repricing, firm crude and divergent Asian cash informs Stress and Confidence rather than Tail, because no persistent one-way NQ structure, shallow-pullback sequence or repeated extension after a failed retracement has been observed. Tail is therefore held in the low band at 12% with Stress lifted to 49%. The shared Finviz context file is about nine days old and was not used as current evidence; research for this run was independent and primary-source based.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 10-14% through the Asian and European hours of Oct 7, rose to a 20-23% WATCH band between 11:00Z and 15:00Z as a trend-down phase developed into the US open, then decayed to 11-18% as the dip to 30,904.46 was fully retraced into the cash close. Stress held a 45-54% elevated band and Confidence stayed in the high band at 87-89%.
outlookSummary: Base case is continued two-way NQ rotation while multi-decade-high long-end yields, firm crude and weaker Asian cash remain the dominant background conflict. Conditional Tail holds 12-13% through the Asian hours, rises to 14-17% across the European session and the 08:30Z Waller speech, reaches a 19-21% peak around the 12:30Z claims block and the 13:30Z US cash open, eases to 18-19% late morning, returns to 20% for the 17:00Z 30-Year Bond Auction, then decays to 12-15% after the 20:00Z cash close. Stress tracks 48-57% with peaks at the open and the auction. The 30-Year auction with the long end near 2002 highs is the clearest credible delayed-second-leg mechanism in the window.
